Principle 15: The Korean Economy
The Korean Economy after the Korean War
By the end of the Korean War, the entire country had been devastated by death and destruction.
Our country’s economy was very unstable.
At that time, I was very young, so I/my parents experienced a very poor life.
By the 1970s, Korea’s economy was showing signs of progress.
The Korean Economy: The Seventies and the Eighties
After the 1970s, our country’s economy started to develop.
During the 1980’s the Olympic games and other cultural events were held in Korea, and the country became known more around the world.
Our economy started to and continued to develop very quickly during these two decades.
The Korean Economy: The Nineties
By the 1990s, instability began as a result of Korea’s rapidly growing economy.
By the end of the decade, Korea’s economy was in crisis.
Koreans worked very diligently to overcome this difficult time.
However, the gap that separated the rich from the poor continued to grow.
The Korean Economy Today
Even in modern times, no country’s economy is completely stable.
This goes for Korea’s economy as well.
As the cost of living increases, so does the price of oil.
This makes life very difficult for us in Korea because we are a very oil dependent nation.
On the bright side, our country’s is exporting more and more of its products every year.
As a citizen of Korean, I’m trying my best to help the economy by not wasting money and following a strict budget.
Hopefully, all Korean people will do their part in improving the economy.
By doing so, we will all financially prosper in the future.
